subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should core support `messages.operationalReplies.redirect` as a fail-closed write to an explicitly authorized operator session, and what recovery behavior is acceptable when that write fails?
rationale: The code changes the disclosure and availability boundary for provider/runtime notices; tests can verify mechanics but cannot choose whether source suppression, retry, or fallback is the intended security contract.

options.title: Approve a fail-closed authorized redirect
options.body: Keep source suppression when the target write fails, but define and enforce the target-session authorization contract and document operator recovery.

options.title: Make redirect recoverable
options.body: Define bounded retry or visible operator recovery semantics before suppressing the source notice, accepting the additional delivery-state complexity.

options.title: Ship only silent and once modes
options.body: Defer redirect until the repository has an approved operator-session authorization and recovery model.

recommendation.title: Approve a fail-closed authorized redirect
recommendation.body: Keep source suppression when the target write fails, but define and enforce the target-session authorization contract and document operator recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this contributor as the current proposal and implementation contact; current-main ownership needs a maintainer-history follow-up.
